meta.title: FAQ
meta.description: The four questions asked most often about React Scheduler: the license, Next.js, using it without the default styles, and the built-in languages.

sections.without-default-styles: Can I use it without the default styles?

free.text: Yes. React Scheduler is MIT licensed, with no paid tier and no feature gating: the package you install is the whole thing, and everything on this site is in it. The full text is on the <link to="/discover-more/license/">License</link> page.

nextjs.text: Yes, in both routers. The schedule reads the viewport and listens for scrolling, so it is a client component: put 'use client' at the top of the file that renders it, or of a wrapper around it. The server still renders its markup, and hydration is silent. Next.js has the details.

unstyled.text: Yes, at three levels. Keep styles.css and change the CSS variables; or import base.css, which carries the structure and nothing else; or pass unstyled and bring your own class names through classNames. Customization shows what each level costs you.

languages.text: Seven: English, Romanian, Hungarian, Spanish, French, German and Portuguese. Each is a plain object exported from @react-schedulerkit/react-scheduler/locales, so you can pass one, extend it, or write your own — dates, times and counts follow the pack's locale through Intl. See Localization.
